newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Teva estimate raised.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Teva estimate raised.

text.p: UBS Ltd said it was raising its 1996 earnings per share (EPS) forecast for Teva Pharmaceutical Industries by $0.05 to $1.37 after the company reported better-than-expected third quarter results.
In the third quarter the Israeli company earned $0.39 a share, up from $0.32 a year earlier. UBS maintained its 1997 estimate of $2.00 and $2.90 for 1998.
UBS director of Israel research Daniel Carasso said good results were achieved despite worldwide price erosion for generic drugs.
He said three recent purchases by Teva in Europe had created near-term uncertainty about the company's earnings.
"The company has emerged from the uncertainty with better-than-expected results and is poised to roll out its growth engine of the next several years, Copaxone," Carasso wrote in a recent report.
Teva is awaiting final U.S. approval for its multiple sclerosis treatment Copaxone.
"Assuming success for Copaxone, Teva's valuation still looks compelling versus both proprietary and generic comparables," Carasso said.

"We assume that Copaxone will account for $0.23 of group EPS in 1997, rising to $1.47 by 2000. On this basis, even after 55 percent price appreciation from its 52-week low, Teva remains a buy," he said.
